text: Mm? Oh, a visitor. Sit, sit. Mind the nets, they've more holes than sense.
You've the look of someone who doesn't know what sea they're sailing on.

menu.text: Ask an old man something, then.

text: We call it the Driftwake. My grandmother said something enormous passed through here, long before anyone.
What we sail on is only the wake it left behind. Currents that don't follow the moon. Islands that drift a little further every year.
Folk laugh. But I've mended nets on this beach sixty years, and the horizon isn't where it used to be.
Fish are clever. They leave before trouble does.
Something's stirring out past the reef. They felt it before we did.
You found one, didn't you. I can see it on you.
They say each stone holds a piece of a route. Find them all and you'll know where the great thing went.
Or why it left. I'm not sure which frightens me more.
